They saw gold nuggets and gold stones in the field.

This happened because of the merit from the good deeds (donations) they had performed.
Alms-giving benefits both the giver’s mind and spirit, and supports the well-being of others.
Being kind, generous, and selfless leads to both spiritual and material blessings.
Both of them happily rejoiced and said “Sadhu” three times to celebrate the other’s good deed.

1. Physical support
2. Better health and comfort
3. Emotional relief
4. More daily stability
5. Stronger community connection
6. Spiritual benefit
Any act of giving food or necessary items to monks with sincerity counts as practical alms-giving.
yes, ive seen many times especially in buddhist temples, and ive donated a few with my family
their good deeds (donations) transformed their life for the better.

What the farmer (Maung Punna) donated:

1. A cup of water
2. A tamarind twig (for the monk to wash his face and brush his teeth)

His wife (Ma Uttara) also donated:
1. The lunch rice she was bringing for her husband.
His wife donated the lunch rice she had originally brought for her husband.
